I have been working this land since I was a child, watching my father and grandfather do it. 4.1 mu is not much, and with some family off working in the city now, I do most of the fieldwork myself. I cannot afford to gamble.

My land splits like this: about 2.5 mu I do wheat in winter and then maize right after harvest — that is the main thing everyone here does. The other 1.6 mu I put in cotton, same as I have done before.

**Wheat** — I plant in mid-October. My neighbor Lao Wang uses that Jimai 22 seed and got a good harvest last year, so I switched to that two seasons ago and it did well. At planting I put down one bag of compound fertilizer across the whole 2.5 mu — that is about 50 jin spread out. Then in March when the plants start to stretch I walk out with another bag of urea and broadcast it. I water three times: once right after planting to help it root in, once in spring, once when heads are filling. I spray for weeds in winter and then spray twice more for rust and aphids before harvest. I use the rotary tiller after maize to turn the stubble under.

**Maize** — Right after I cut the wheat in June I drop the maize seed in. No plowing — just seed it straight. I use that Xianyu 335 hybrid because everyone around here uses it and it fills well. One bag of compound at planting across the 2.5 mu, then I throw another bag of urea when the plant is knee-high. I only water twice unless there is a real dry spell — once around planting and once at silking. Two sprays for corn borer and earworm.

**Cotton** — This takes more work. I plow it in spring before planting. Cotton here needs feeding in stages — base fertilizer, then top up twice during boll setting. I also have to spray a lot, six or seven times, because if the bollworm gets in I lose the whole thing. Four waterings — spring before planting, then during flowering, boll setting, and one more if August is dry. I use the improved hybrid variety from the shop in town — costs more but the yield difference is real.

My biggest worry is the cotton pesticide bill. If I cut corners there I lose money on the whole crop. The wheat and maize fertilizer I do not change much — same bags as last year, same schedule.
